$comment: Impact-dimension ontology for M4I. Dimensions mirror the topical buckets of docs/calibration-corpus-sources.md. Each leaf category carries the questions that touch that impact dimension; the calibration harness uses them as retrieval probes.

dimensions.name: Political & governance
dimensions.definition: Changes involving political institutions, policy, governance, regulation, or public decision-making.

categories.name: Advocacy & policy influence
categories.definition: Efforts or changes intended to influence laws, policies, political agendas, or public decision-makers.
include: adoption of a standard or guideline
exclude: general public awareness without a policy objective
questions: What policy or legislative change did this work seek to bring about, and was it adopted?
Which government bodies or decision-makers were engaged, and what did they commit to?
What evidence shows a recommendation was taken up in law, regulation, or official guidance?
How is the influence of this work on the policy agenda measured or reported?

categories.name: Governance & institutional capacity
categories.definition: Changes in the capability, accountability, transparency, or integrity of public institutions.
exclude: purely financial performance of an institution
questions: How did the capacity of the responsible public institution change as a result of the intervention?
What accountability, audit, or transparency mechanisms were introduced or strengthened?
Which indicators track improvements in governance quality or institutional performance?
What evidence is reported on corruption, integrity, or misuse of public resources?

categories.name: Civic participation & representation
categories.definition: Changes in how citizens participate in, or are represented within, public decision-making.
questions: How did citizen or community participation in decision-making change?
Which groups gained or lost representation in governing or consultative bodies?
What consultation processes were run, and how were their results used?
How is civic space or freedom of association reported to have changed?

dimensions.name: Economy & finance
dimensions.definition: Changes in economic activity, incomes, employment, fiscal conditions, or access to finance and markets.

categories.name: Livelihoods, employment & income
categories.definition: Changes in jobs, earnings, productivity, or the security of household livelihoods.
questions: How many jobs were created, sustained, or lost, and for whom?
What change in household income or earnings is reported, and over what period?
How did labour productivity or business performance change among participants?
Which indicators measure the quality or security of employment, not just its quantity?

categories.name: Macroeconomic & fiscal conditions
categories.definition: Changes in aggregate economic conditions, public finances, debt, inflation, or monetary policy.
questions: What change in growth, inflation, or the fiscal balance is projected or observed?
How is the sustainability of public debt assessed, and against which thresholds?
Which macroeconomic indicators are used to judge whether the reform succeeded?
What fiscal cost or saving is attributed to the measure described?

categories.name: Market access & financial inclusion
categories.definition: Changes in the ability of people or firms to reach markets, credit, insurance, or payment systems.
questions: How did access to credit, savings, or insurance change for the target population?
What barriers to market participation were removed, and with what measured effect?
Which indicators track financial inclusion, and how are they disaggregated?
What evidence shows small enterprises reaching new buyers or markets?

dimensions.name: Social impact
dimensions.definition: Changes in wellbeing, equity, social relations, and access to essential services.

categories.name: Health & wellbeing
categories.definition: Changes in physical or mental health, nutrition, mortality, or subjective wellbeing.
exclude: health sector budget lines without a health outcome
questions: What change in health status, mortality, or morbidity is reported?
How did nutrition or food security outcomes change for the affected population?
Which health indicators are tracked, and at what frequency?
What evidence links the intervention to a measured wellbeing outcome rather than service delivery alone?

categories.name: Equity, inclusion & social cohesion
categories.definition: Changes in the distribution of benefits across groups, in discrimination, or in relations between groups.
exclude: formal legal rights without evidence of practice
questions: How were benefits or harms distributed across gender, age, disability, or ethnic groups?
What change in an inequality or disparity measure is reported?
Which indicators capture inclusion of marginalised groups, and how are they disaggregated?
What evidence describes changes in trust or relations between communities?

categories.name: Access to basic services
categories.definition: Changes in the availability, affordability, or quality of essential services such as water, sanitation, energy, and social protection.
questions: How many people gained access to the service, and how was access defined?
What change in service reliability, quality, or affordability is documented?
Which coverage indicators are used, and what is the baseline against which they are compared?
What evidence shows the service reached the poorest or hardest-to-reach households?

dimensions.name: Environment & climate
dimensions.definition: Changes in emissions, climate risk, ecosystems, pollution, or the use of natural resources.

categories.name: Emissions & climate mitigation
categories.definition: Changes in greenhouse gas emissions or in the activities and commitments that drive them.
questions: What greenhouse gas emission reduction is claimed, and how was it calculated?
Which mitigation target or commitment does this document set or report against?
How much renewable capacity or energy saving is attributed to the intervention?
What indicators are used to monitor progress towards the emissions goal?

categories.name: Climate resilience & adaptation
categories.definition: Changes in exposure or vulnerability to climate hazards, and in the capacity to adapt to them.
questions: Which climate hazards are identified, and how is vulnerability to them measured?
What adaptation measures were implemented, and what risk reduction is claimed?
How is the resilience of communities or assets assessed before and after?
What early warning or preparedness capability was established?

categories.name: Ecosystems, pollution & natural resources
categories.definition: Changes in biodiversity, land, water, air quality, or the sustainable use of natural resources.
questions: What change in habitat area, biodiversity, or ecosystem condition is reported?
How did pollutant concentrations or water quality change, and against which standard?
Which natural resource indicators are monitored, and by whom?
What evidence documents land restoration or degradation attributable to the project?

dimensions.name: Urban structures & transport
dimensions.definition: Changes in mobility, infrastructure, land use, housing, and the built environment of cities and regions.

categories.name: Mobility & transport access
categories.definition: Changes in how people and goods move, and in who can reach destinations and services.
questions: What change in travel time, ridership, or mode share is reported?
How did access to jobs, schools, or health facilities change for residents?
Which mobility indicators are measured, and over what network or corridor?
What evidence shows the change in service benefited transport-disadvantaged groups?

categories.name: Infrastructure condition & investment
categories.definition: Changes in the physical state, safety, or capital funding of transport and urban infrastructure.
include: asset condition and state of good repair
questions: What change in asset condition or state of good repair is documented?
How did crash, injury, or fatality counts change after the intervention?
Which performance targets govern the infrastructure investment described?
What maintenance backlog or capital need is quantified?

categories.name: Land use, housing & urban planning
categories.definition: Changes in spatial planning, housing supply and affordability, and the organisation of urban development.
questions: What land use or zoning change is proposed, and what development does it enable?
How did housing supply or affordability change in the area studied?
Which planning indicators are used to evaluate the spatial strategy?
What evidence addresses displacement or the distributional effects of redevelopment?

dimensions.name: Humanitarian concerns, law & rights
dimensions.definition: Changes in protection of people in crisis, in human rights, and in compliance with legal and normative frameworks.

categories.name: Protection & human rights
categories.definition: Changes in the safety, dignity, and rights of people, particularly those exposed to violence, displacement, or discrimination.
questions: Which rights or protection risks are identified, and for which population?
What change in the safety or legal status of affected people is reported?
How is access to justice, remedy, or redress measured?
What evidence documents violations and the response to them?

categories.name: Humanitarian needs & response
categories.definition: Assessment of needs arising from crisis, and the reach, quality, and accountability of assistance provided.
questions: What humanitarian needs were assessed, and how severe are they judged to be?
How many affected people were reached with assistance, and with what gap remaining?
Which indicators measure the timeliness or adequacy of the response?
What feedback from affected populations is reported, and how was it acted on?

categories.name: Legal frameworks & normative compliance
categories.definition: Changes in law, treaty obligation, or normative standards, and in the degree to which actors comply with them.
exclude: political advocacy without a legal instrument
questions: Which legal instrument or normative standard applies, and what does it require?
What change in national law or its implementation is documented?
How is compliance with the obligation monitored and reported?
What judicial or quasi-judicial findings are cited, and what remedy did they order?

dimensions.name: Education
dimensions.definition: Changes in access to education, in learning, and in the capacity of education systems.

categories.name: Access & participation
categories.definition: Changes in enrolment, attendance, retention, and completion across education levels.
questions: What change in enrolment, attendance, or completion is reported, and for which cohort?
Which groups remain excluded from education, and what barriers are identified?
How are participation indicators defined and disaggregated?
What evidence shows dropout was reduced rather than merely delayed?

categories.name: Learning outcomes & quality
categories.definition: Changes in what learners know and can do, and in the instructional quality that produces it.
questions: What change in learning achievement is measured, and with which assessment?
How large is the reported learning gain, and how was it estimated?
Which indicators of instructional quality are collected?
What evidence connects the curriculum or pedagogy change to a learning outcome?

categories.name: Teachers & system capacity
categories.definition: Changes in the education workforce, in school management, and in the financing and administration of education systems.
questions: What change in teacher supply, qualification, or retention is reported?
How did professional development alter classroom practice, and how was that verified?
Which system-level indicators track education financing or administration?
What evidence describes the capacity of the ministry or district to monitor schools?
